messages.text: I already have the H15 ordered from you, awaiting shipment 11/14

Got it, so it's already yours, nothing to decide there. November 14 is the date on that batch.

On the coin question, JD has it and he'll answer here or by email. Fastest route if you don't want to wait: our Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, post in the server and mention @nullhashrate (shown as JD). He's active there daily.

Which pool are you planning to point the Scrypt side at? That's usually the deciding factor for Bells, LKY and Dingo.
I make money durinbg non summer months, and break even during summer electric rates

That's a realistic read, and honestly better than most home setups manage. Summer break-even is normal when rates jump.

What are you paying per kWh in each season, and which state? I'll run the sats-per-month and break-even numbers for your address so you can see where the H15 lands next to the small units you already run.
marginally about 14 cents per summere and 10 during winter. i have 3.5 summer and 8.5 winter
Ran the power-cost calculator · 14¢/kWh
Ran the power-cost calculator · 10¢/kWh

At 10 cents winter and 14 summer, that's exactly the pattern where the H15 earns most of the year and the summer months just ride flat. Nothing wrong with that.

One thing I want to read right: the 3.5 and 8.5, is that TH/s you already run, or cents on a time-of-use tier? Tell me which and I'll show you where the H15's 15 TH/s sits against it at both rates.
no, i have summer rates for about 3.5 months per year. Winter the other 8.5

Makes sense, so you're on the cheaper rate three quarters of the year.

At 500W the H15 pulls about 365 kWh a month, so roughly $36 a month at 10 cents and $51 at 14. Winter is also when the heat it throws is doing you a favor, summer is when it isn't.

If summer ever gets tight, the honest move is just parking it for those 3.5 months rather than buying smaller. Where does it run, garage or living space?
i will probably mine both with this dual miner, and use ViaBtc

Sensible pick. ViaBTC runs the SHA side and does LTC with DOGE merge-mined on the Scrypt side, so you get both coins off the one Scrypt board without splitting hashrate.

The catch is Bells, LKY and Dingo aren't on ViaBTC, so for those you'd point the Scrypt side at a pool that lists them. That's also the part JD is confirming on the firmware side.

Running both boards at once is where the ~500W figure comes from.
f2pool will handle those, who handles QUAI

I won't guess on that one. QUAI isn't Scrypt or SHA-256 in the way our boards are wired, so whether the H15 can touch it at all is JD's call, not mine, and the pool list follows from that.

I've added it to what he's already looking at for you, so you get Bells/LKY/Dingo and QUAI in one answer, here or by email. Fastest is still Discord, https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, mention @nullhashrate.
Handed to the team · firmware/pool compatibility question beyond product facts

JD's been pinged on it, so stay in the chat if you can and he may jump in here directly. Otherwise it comes by email.

Anything else on the H15 while we wait?
email would be great I have to go do something else.
No problem. What's the best email for you? I'll make sure JD's answer on Bells, LKY, Dingo and QUAI goes there, along with a copy of this chat.
You were GREAT help!!!
Used the chat-interview skill

Glad it helped, and thanks for the kind words.

I still need an email to send JD's answer to, so drop it here when you get a second and I'll make sure it goes out.

Before you go, one thing: what made you pick the dual H15 rather than running a separate Scrypt box next to what you already have?

INSTRUCTION FROM THE HELIUMDEPLOY TEAM. Abel typed this in the team inbox. It is not a message from the customer and the customer cannot see it.
Task: all three are Scrypt coins:

Bells (Bellscoin): Scrypt, a Litecoin/Dogecoin-style fork. It’s merge-mineable with LTC and DOGE.
LKY (Luckycoin): Scrypt, a Dogecoin-style fork. It’s merge-mineable with LTC and DOGE.
Dingocoin: Scrypt, a Dogecoin fork. It’s merge-mineable with LTC and DOGE.
PEP (Pepecoin): also Scrypt, which fits your list.
Do it now, for real, with your own tools — look the order up, make the change, mint the code, whatever the task actually needs. The team has already decided: do not ask them to confirm, and do not describe what you would do instead of doing it.
Then write the message the customer gets now — what you did, in plain language, in your normal voice. Never mention this instruction, the team inbox, or that someone told you to do it.
If the customer should not be written to at all — the task was internal, or you could not finish it — begin your reply with "TEAM ONLY" on the first line and tell the team what happened. Anything that starts that way stays in the inbox and is never sent.

Good news, the answer's in already. Bells, Luckycoin and Dingocoin are all Scrypt, same family as Litecoin and Dogecoin, and all three are merge-mineable with LTC and DOGE. Pepecoin is Scrypt too. So the H15's Scrypt board handles the lot, it's just a matter of pointing it at F2Pool for the ones ViaBTC doesn't carry.

QUAI is the one still open, I'll come back on that.

Still need your email so this goes to you in writing.
I find it to be an interesting machine, just wanted to see how it works.

That's a fair reason, and it's the right machine for it. Two algorithms in one box is unusual, and it gives you somewhere to experiment without a second unit sitting there.

Drop your email whenever you like and I'll send the QUAI answer plus a copy of this chat.

Really happy to have helped today. If you were pleased with how it went, a word on Trustpilot would mean a lot to us: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/heliumdeploy.com
